note: Conformance cases for x402 delivery declarations. Each case gives an input body and the properties an implementation must derive from it. An implementation passes a case when every field in `expect` matches. Fields not listed are not constrained.

cases.why: Provider declares age in seconds. Must be read as seconds.
Provider declares age in milliseconds. Must be converted to seconds and rounded to the nearest second, on every path: an adapter and a heuristic reading the same field must not disagree.
Provider states its own data is stale. Must be surfaced.
Provider broke what it declared: not usable, and the provider is at fault.
Provider delivered what it declared; the caller's policy was stricter. Not the provider's fault, and the charge stands.
Nothing recognisable. Absence of a declaration is information, not an error. Must not invent values.
A field inferred from its name is never reported as a declaration, and is rounded to the nearest second like any other path.
A numeric field with no recognisable unit suffix must not be interpreted.
Normalisation is never lossy. The original body must survive.
